title: Azure Fundamentals: One Lunch at a Time
tagline: Learn every fundamental Azure service in 31 lunch breaks.

seasons.name: Season 1 · The Pantry Server
seasons.blurb: One tired server, one unanswered question. Twenty-one lunches to move Nusantara Retail into Azure and answer the director with numbers.

seasons.name: Season 2 · After the Answer
seasons.blurb: The shop survived. Now come the auditors, the 12.12 sale, ransomware and a merger. Ten lunches that turn a working setup into a professional one.

cast.name: Ibu Sari
cast.quote: No surprise bills. I want to be able to explain every rupiah.
cast.bio: Runs Nusantara Retail. Asks one question until somebody answers it with numbers.

cast.name: Pak Budi
cast.quote: Head office has used 10.0.0.0/16 for twelve years. Please don't overlap it.
cast.bio: Knows every cable in the building. Takes the backup USB drive home on Fridays — when he remembers.

cast.name: Dewi
cast.quote: Give me a platform. I don't want to patch servers ever again.
cast.bio: Writes the storefront. Spends more Friday nights patching servers than she would like.

cast.name: Rizky
cast.quote: Could you open SSH from anywhere — just for a week?
cast.bio: Helpful, fast, and the reason the course has a lunch about least privilege.

cast.name: You
cast.bio: Hired to move the shop into Azure — and to answer the question nobody could.

director.question: If that server dies, how long can't we sell?

01.ep: The Room Next to the Pantry
01.hook: One tired server, one unanswered question, and a director who wants no surprise bills.
01.outcome: you set up a safe Azure lab — with a budget alarm — before spending a single rupiah.

badge.name: Lab Ready
badge.desc: Set up your lab, tools and cost guardrails.

02.hook: Finance has a quote for a bigger server. The director wants the cloud explained in money and in risk.
02.outcome: you explained IaaS, PaaS and SaaS — and who is responsible for what — in money and in risk.

badge.name: Cloud Fluent
badge.desc: Explain the cloud in money and in risk.

02.answer: Days — and we pay for that server whether we sell or not.

03.hook: Jakarta or Singapore? And what happens when that building has a bad day?
03.outcome: you chose a home region and saw how availability zones survive a datacenter failure.

badge.name: Region Scout
badge.desc: Choose regions and zones with confidence.

03.answer: Still days today. In Azure, a whole datacenter could fail without stopping us.

04.hook: Three weeks of experiments, no naming rules, and nobody knows what belongs to the shop.
04.outcome: you organised subscriptions, resource groups, tags and locks so every rupiah has an owner.

badge.name: Tidy Architect
badge.desc: Organise Azure with scopes, tags and locks.

04.answer: Still days — but now we know exactly what we own in Azure.

05.hook: A contractor starts on Monday, and the easy option is to share a login.
05.outcome: you gave Rizky exactly the access he needs — and a clean way to take it back.

badge.name: Gatekeeper
badge.desc: Grant least-privilege access with Azure RBAC.

05.answer: Still days — but only the right people can touch the new setup.

06.hook: A desk fan in front of the server is not a strategy. Time to get the shop off that box.
06.outcome: the storefront runs on its first Azure VM — and stops paying for compute when it is deallocated.

badge.name: First Server
badge.desc: Build and run your first Azure VM.

06.answer: If the VM dies, I can rebuild it in about ten minutes.

07.ep: The USB Drive Goes Home on Fridays
07.hook: Forty thousand photos and ten years of invoices live on one disk next to the pantry.
07.outcome: photos, invoices and price lists now live in redundant storage, on the right access tier.

badge.name: Data Keeper
badge.desc: Store data with the right redundancy and tier.

07.answer: Minutes to rebuild the server — and our files are stored at least three times.

08.hook: Pak Budi's 10.0.0.0/16 must never clash — and Rizky wants SSH open to the whole internet.
08.outcome: you planned the address space and locked traffic down with NSGs and explicit outbound access.

badge.name: Network Planner
badge.desc: Plan address spaces and filter traffic.

08.answer: Minutes to rebuild — and the app tier can't even be seen from the internet.

09.hook: A perfectly good twin server sits idle while shoppers can only find one.
09.outcome: a Standard load balancer now keeps the shop open when a server — or a whole zone — fails.

badge.name: Always Open
badge.desc: Keep selling when a server fails.

09.answer: If one server dies, customers don't even notice.

10.hook: Patching servers every Friday night is not what a developer was hired for.
10.outcome: the storefront moved to App Service: no operating system to patch, and releases swap in with no downtime.

badge.name: Platform Pilot
badge.desc: Run web apps without managing servers.

10.answer: A server failure goes unnoticed, and there are no servers left to patch.

11.hook: The orders still live on SQL Express, guarded by a shared password and a USB drive.
11.outcome: orders now live in Azure SQL, with Entra-only sign-in and automatic backups.

badge.name: Order Keeper
badge.desc: Run a managed relational database.

11.answer: A failed server goes unnoticed, and orders can be restored to almost any point in the past week.

12.hook: Every new product type means another late-night schema change.
12.outcome: the product catalogue lives in Cosmos DB, partitioned to scale for the 12.12 rush.

badge.name: Catalogue Wrangler
badge.desc: Model and partition NoSQL data.

12.answer: Failures go unnoticed, orders are restorable, and the catalogue scales on demand.

13.hook: The most expensive sentence in the office.
13.outcome: the storefront ships as a container that scales from zero with Container Apps.

badge.name: Ship It
badge.desc: Package and run containers on Azure.

13.answer: Failures go unnoticed, and the same container runs identically everywhere.

14.ep: When the Courier API Slows Down
14.hook: One slow partner shouldn't slow down every checkout.
14.outcome: orders flow through queues and functions, so a slow partner no longer blocks checkout.

badge.name: Event Driven
badge.desc: Decouple work with events and functions.

14.answer: Failures go unnoticed — even when a partner's API is slow.

15.ep: The Password in the Zip File
15.hook: A database password went out in a chat message — and it has been in Git for two years.
15.outcome: secrets live in Key Vault, apps sign in with managed identities, and defence comes in layers.

badge.name: Secret Keeper
badge.desc: Protect secrets and defend in depth.

15.answer: Failures go unnoticed, and a leaked file no longer leaks a password.

16.hook: Instagram noticed the slowdown forty minutes before you did.
16.outcome: alerts reach you before customers notice, and the activity log answers "who did it?".

badge.name: Early Warning
badge.desc: Alert on trouble before customers notice.

16.answer: We know within minutes when something breaks — usually before customers do.

17.hook: A neighbour lost everything because the attackers deleted the backups first. Have we ever tested a restore?
17.outcome: you ran a real restore drill and protected the backups with soft delete.

badge.name: Restore Drill Survivor
badge.desc: Back up, restore and plan for disaster.

17.answer: Even if someone deletes everything, we restore — and we have practised it.

18.ep: A Storage Account in West Europe
18.hook: Untagged resources, data in the wrong region, and nothing stopped anyone.
18.outcome: Azure Policy now blocks the wrong regions and adds the tags people forget.

badge.name: Rule Maker
badge.desc: Enforce rules with Azure Policy.

18.answer: We recover from deletions, and guardrails stop the mistakes that cause them.

19.hook: The first real Azure bill arrives, and it is bigger than the spreadsheet.
19.outcome: every cost has an owner, the waste is gone, and a budget watches the rest.

badge.name: Rupiah Ranger
badge.desc: Find, explain and control cloud costs.

19.answer: We stay online — and we can explain every rupiah it costs.

20.ep: Rebuild It All in an Hour?
20.hook: The whole design lives in people's memories, and memories don't redeploy.
20.outcome: the environment now lives in a Bicep file you can rebuild on demand.

badge.name: Infra Coder
badge.desc: Describe infrastructure as code.

20.answer: We stay online, and we can rebuild the whole environment from code.

21.hook: The monthly meeting is on Friday. The director wants a straight answer — with numbers.
21.outcome: you answered the director: a server or a zone can fail and we keep selling, and deleted orders come back in minutes.

badge.name: Core Graduate
badge.desc: Design, build and defend the core platform.

21.answer: A server or a zone fails: we keep selling. Deleted orders: back in minutes. A whole region: hours — less with a standby.

22.hook: An expired pipeline secret, five permanent Owners and a contractor who never really left.
22.outcome: pipelines sign in without secrets, and admins get access only when they need it.

badge.name: Zero Standing Access
badge.desc: Remove secrets and standing admin rights.

22.answer: Same answer as Friday — and nobody holds keys they don't need right now.

23.hook: Last year the server froze seven minutes after midnight, and the flash sale ended before it began.
23.outcome: a zone-spanning scale set grows for the sale and shrinks afterwards — with nobody awake at midnight.

badge.name: Autoscaler
badge.desc: Scale VMs across zones automatically.

23.answer: We keep selling through failures — and through the 12.12 rush.

24.hook: A supplier's files were held to ransom overnight. Could ours be next?
24.outcome: invoices are versioned, immutable and reachable only through a private endpoint.

badge.name: Immutable
badge.desc: Protect data against deletion and ransomware.

24.answer: We keep selling, and our invoices can't be altered or encrypted — not even by an insider.

25.hook: Finance wants its own network, and the auditor wants proof of what can talk to it.
25.outcome: a hub-and-spoke network sends spoke-to-spoke traffic through an inspection point you control.

badge.name: Hub Builder
badge.desc: Design hub-and-spoke networks with routing.

25.answer: We keep selling, and every network path is one we chose and can inspect.

26.hook: Forty stores upload their sales over the internet — and one upload failed three nights in a row.
26.outcome: head office and Azure talk through an encrypted tunnel, with a plan for when the line drops.

badge.name: Bridge Builder
badge.desc: Connect on-premises networks to Azure.

26.answer: We keep selling, and head office reaches Azure privately — with a plan B.

27.hook: Attack strings fill the logs, and shoppers in Makassar wait on Jakarta.
27.outcome: a web application firewall blocks the attacks, and traffic finds the healthy origin.

badge.name: Firewall at the Gate
badge.desc: Route and protect web traffic at layer 7.

27.answer: We keep selling through failures and attacks, and shoppers reach a healthy origin.

28.hook: How long can't we sell — and how many orders do we lose — if a whole region fails?
28.outcome: a failover group moves the orders database to a second region in minutes, losing only seconds of data.

badge.name: Failover Ready
badge.desc: Fail a database over to another region.

28.answer: Even if the whole region goes dark: selling again in minutes, losing only seconds of orders.

29.hook: Four services, a vendor's Helm chart, and a director who won't hire a team to babysit servers.
29.outcome: a small AKS cluster heals itself, scales and rolls out updates — and you know what it costs at 3 a.m.

badge.name: Cluster Captain
badge.desc: Run workloads on Azure Kubernetes Service.

29.answer: Region down: minutes. And the microservices heal themselves.

30.ep: Why Was Checkout Slow on Friday?
30.hook: The CPU was fine. Checkout took four seconds. 312 carts were abandoned.
30.outcome: logs, metrics and traces meet in one workspace, and a KQL query finds the real cause.

badge.name: KQL Detective
badge.desc: Find root causes with Log Analytics and KQL.

30.answer: Region down: minutes. And when checkout slows, we find out why within the hour.

31.hook: Guardrails that protect one subscription won't survive a merger.
31.outcome: management groups and policy-as-code now govern every subscription — including the new ones.

badge.name: Governance at Scale
badge.desc: Govern many subscriptions as code.

31.answer: Minutes for a regional outage, seconds of data at risk — and the same rules everywhere we run.

finale.hook: No guided steps. Design it, build it, prove it.

badge.name: Architect
badge.desc: Complete the advanced capstone challenge.
